source_read: https://fathippo.co.uk/menus/food/, /menus/drinks/, /menus/kids/, /menus/special-menu/ (each dish's modal: Allergy Information, one block per part with its allergens and a 'May Contain' list) and https://fathippo.co.uk/allergens/. robots.txt: 'User-agent: *' with an empty Allow, nothing disallowed (RFC 9309 matcher). The four menu pages were downloaded again on 2026-10-09 and are byte-identical to the 2026-10-08 copies the data was built from (sha256 food e969bfe5..., drinks e2f81960..., kids a23db84d..., special-menu 8085d610...), so checked_on stays 2026-10-08.
method: tools/uk_extract/fat_hippo.py reads the saved HTML with regexes and requires each card's own allergen list to equal the union of its parts. Verification used a different path: Chromium (Playwright) loaded the live pages, opened every dish modal as a visitor would (clicking the info button and every 'May Contain' toggle) and took each part's rendered innerText (169 cards); a separate script (no regexes on HTML, its own word table) rebuilt contains / may contain / named cereals for every card and compared them with allergens.csv. 17 modals were also screenshotted and read by eye (Five Lies, Big Poppa special menu, Freddies Fingers: Crack, Little Lies among them; Superfries Me! and Sprite Zero to confirm the empty parts).
held_back_detail: No allergen statement for a part, not even 'No Known Allergens' (7): Trash Browns, Big Poppa and Wild Bill (part 'Jalapenos'), Uncle Phil (part 'Caramelised Onions & Green Peppers'), Superfries Me! (upgrade) and Gimme S'more! (each has a part with no name and no text: the descriptions list Parmesan and chocolate sauce, which no part names), Sprite Zero (its only part). Their lines are in holdback.csv and they get no allergens.csv row, so deleting the line stops the build rather than publishing an incomplete list. Row contradicts the dish (1, policy 3): Chocolate Brownie Milkshake (kids upgrade): part 'Chocolate Brownie Crumb' with no gluten marked. The other 34 held-back dishes are held for their numbers only and keep their complete allergen row (ignored while held).
audit: check_chain.py fat-hippo --fail-on-high: 0 errors, 0 high, 0 medium allergen or nutrition audit flags (8 pre-existing drink warnings about kcal vs macros). A part-by-part scan of all 169 cards for names that contradict their own allergens (butter/cheese/cream with no milk, cookie/crumb/bun/batter with no gluten, mayo/aioli with no egg, vegan with milk/egg) found only items already held back, or parts whose dish still lists the allergen through another part: Garlic & Herb Butter and Smoked Chilli Butter print 'No Known Allergens' / no milk, but every dish using them (Freddies Fingers: Crack, Triple G, Corn Ribs) lists milk from another part, so no published dish row is wrong on milk; vegan cheese slice, vegan mayo, Biscoff Butter and Peanut Butter print no milk/egg, consistent with their ingredients.
notes: may_contain_published = yes (every part prints a 'May Contain' list). Garlic and Onion are printed as allergens by the page but are not among the 14, so they are not published. 'Cereal - Gluten' is the only gluten wording that appears in a 'contains' list (Barley only appears in may-contain lists), so no cereal is named. Nuts and Peanuts are generic; Lupin appears on 3 dishes. Fat Hippo's allergens page also says 'all dishes may contain traces of nuts, as peanuts are present on the premises': a kitchen-wide statement the data contract has no field for, so it is the last sentence of note.txt, not added to the per-dish rows. This change in fat_hippo.py replaces an earlier uncommitted version that DROPPED the 7 dishes from items.csv and images.csv: they are now held back as everywhere else, so items.csv and images.csv are identical to HEAD. The older data/audit/verified/fat-hippo.json (nutrition) still says no allergens are published; this file supersedes that remark.
